paper_metadata.title: Hot tensile characteristics and microstructure of a Cu-0.65Cr-0.08Zr alloy for fusion reactor applications

evidence.quote: The present work deals with high temperature tensile characteristics (in unirradiated conditions) of the heat treatable Cu-0.65 wt'% Cr-0.08 wt% Zr alloy.

the presence (fig. 7b) of equiaxed grains and straight twins and the absence of substructure indicate that the alloy has recrystallized in part statically during the cooling period of the tensile specimens after fracture.

mechanisms.material_state: solution treated, cold worked and aged

evidence.quote: These properties can be attributed to the hardening effect of the very fine and stable intergranular precipitates (fig. 3) through their interaction with the dislocation structure.

mechanisms.name: precipitate coarsening and loss of coherency

evidence.quote: The softening occurred gradually in the alloy beginning at 460 o C (precipitation hardening temperature), because of a coarsening and loss of coherency of the small precipitates and recovery and recrystallization of the worked matrix.

This embrittlement, according to microstructural investigations (optical microscopy and scanning electron microscopy) on several deformed specimens, is due to an intergranular cracking process, which is typical of several copper alloys when hot deformed.
